candidate: Deep LDL-C lowering to guideline target with approved agents
best_trial: CTT meta-analysis + FOURIER/ODYSSEY; oral PCSK9 inhibitor now approved
result: 22% relative risk reduction per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction, reproducible across statins, ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors
effect_unit: relative reduction in major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL-C
effect_display: 22.0% relative reduction in major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL-C
licenses: the strongest quantitative claim available in IHD: lowering LDL-C by a given amount lowers event rate by a predictable proportion, and the effect is additive with baseline risk
does_not_license: it does not reverse established scar or restore myocardium; it slows the process. It also does not remove residual risk - roughly two thirds of events in treated patients are not prevented

best_trial: COLCOT, LoDoCo2, CLEAR SYNERGY; Cochrane review 2025
result: about 9 fewer myocardial infarctions and 8 fewer strokes per 1,000 treated; no effect on cardiovascular mortality; CLEAR SYNERGY neutral in acute coronary syndrome
licenses: guideline backing: ESC 2024 chronic coronary syndrome Class IIa Level A; ACC/AHA Class IIb. The only anti-inflammatory with a positive outcome signal and a guideline place
does_not_license: it does not reduce cardiovascular mortality, it is a Class IIa or IIb recommendation rather than Class I, the recent large ACS trial was neutral, and gastrointestinal adverse events increase
source: ESC 2024 CCS guidelines; Cochrane 2025; CLEAR SYNERGY; Rossello 2025

tier: randomised outcome evidence, neutral or refuted
best_trial: ZEUS (NCT05021835), plus HERMES and ATHENA stopped for futility
result: NEUTRAL: HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.88-1.11) despite hsCRP falling 64% and IL-6 falling 76%; serious infections 20% vs 18%
licenses: a refutation, in 6,385 patients, of the proposition that suppressing IL-6 and CRP in high-risk ASCVD reduces events. Target engagement was demonstrated and benefit was not
does_not_license: it does not prove inflammation is irrelevant - the population had advanced disease and the intervention was downstream. It does show that lowering the marker is not sufficient
source: ZEUS, reported 31 July 2026, published NEJM; HERMES/ATHENA termination September 2026

tier: randomised evidence on a surrogate only
best_trial: CORALreef Lipids and HeFH; CORALreef Outcomes running
result: LDL-C -56% vs placebo at week 24, sustained to week 52; FDA approved 16 July 2026
licenses: attains injectable-antibody LDL-C lowering as a once-daily tablet, which is the adherence problem solved without an irreversible edit
does_not_license: the outcome trial has completed enrolment and not reported; approval rests on the surrogate, exactly as the transfer gate warns
source: NEJM 2026 (CORALreef Lipids); FDA approval 16 July 2026; CORALreef Outcomes NCT06008756

candidate: VERVE-102 in vivo PCSK9 base editing
tier: randomised evidence on a surrogate only
best_trial: Heart-2 (NCT06164730), phase 1b, open-label, single ascending dose
result: LDL-C -62% at 1.0 mg/kg (-78 mg/dL), PCSK9 -88%, durable to 18 months, no treatment-related serious adverse events
licenses: the largest durable LDL-C reduction from a single intervention, on a mechanism that already has outcome support through other agents
does_not_license: its own outcome benefit is unproven and the edit is irreversible. An approved oral PCSK9 inhibitor now produces a similar LDL-C reduction without a permanent edit, which removes most of the practical case for the editing route
source: NEJM 2026 (Heart-2, n=35, open-label); Lilly press release 25 May 2026

result: LVEF +3.9 pp (90% CI 0.9-6.8) uncontrolled; second trial n=8 +4.3 pp, p=0.156. Both below the 6 pp surrogate threshold
licenses: a signal worth testing in a randomised trial with an outcome endpoint, and nothing beyond that
does_not_license: it cannot separate a real effect from natural history or regression to the mean: 20 patients, no control, and an effect below the threshold at which LVEF change predicts mortality benefit

candidate: Combined architecture (cell patch + base editing + OMT)
tier: mechanism or magnitude claim with no clinical outcome data
best_trial: none - never administered together in a controlled setting
result: no clinical data; corrected 20,000-draw estimates are 57.70% for ATLAS-5 and 57.81% for the re-optimized simulation-only ATLAS-5F; neither is robust
licenses: a hypothesis, and an ordered experiment list
does_not_license: it cannot claim the sum of its parts. The repository measured 15 pairwise interactions and refused 14.08 pp of double-counted benefit, and the wider re-search found no robust composition
